notes:
- A detail lands on the right medium: The fold that pushes a freshly fetched detail into the card behind an open sheet matched on the media id alone, so where an anime and a manga share a number one title's synopsis, cover and banner could appear on the other's card until the next recompute. It matches the media type as well now.
- Recent updates counts anime and manga apart: The activity tile deduplicated the week by bare AniList id, so a manga and an anime sharing a number collapsed into one row and the count came up short. Titles are keyed by namespace now.
- A reopened title keeps its detail without asking again: The detail cache's timestamp map was trimmed by iteration order rather than by age, so the entry written last could lose its timestamp; a missing timestamp reads as never fetched, and that title then re-requested its detail on every open for the rest of the session.
- Progress never reads 3 / 0 eps: watchFractionLabel had no positive-total guard while watchFraction and progressCountLabel both had one, so a show whose length AniList has not announced printed its watched count against zero.
- The grid's progress pill stops captioning zero: A zero episode or chapter count is AniList's way of saying the length is not announced, and the new grid passed it into the pill as a length.
- An airing card stops claiming 0 eps: The meta line under the arriving card's status chip used a zero episode count as a length; it now falls back to the episode number, then to Airing now.
- Release notes keep their category in every language: The tone is inferred after lowercasing the title with the device locale, and on a Turkic locale the uppercase I folds differently, so a fix matched no keyword and drew as a plain note.
- A YouTube link in capitals embeds: The composer found the watch wrapper case-insensitively and then cut the string case-sensitively, so a link in capitals was recognised but never reduced to its id.
- An undated message no longer opens the conversation: The bubble list sorted a message with no timestamp above every dated one; it sorts to the end now.
- Quoting a comment names the person once: The already-mentioned test was case-sensitive against the author's name while the reply-to half of it was not, so quoting @Bild credited the name above a line that already said it.
- A banner preview shows the whole banner: Choosing Banner in the Details page editor used to preview the wide key visual cropped into a portrait card, so its left and right thirds were simply not there - the preview showed a slice of the artwork and the reader had to guess at the rest. The preview now draws the banner through the same pannable artwork the profile banner uses: it covers the card with no gap and slowly sweeps across the picture, so the whole banner is reachable, and the blur and tint still apply to it.\n- The Nova hero keeps its artwork inside the hero: The hero artwork is over-covered and drifts against the scroll, and that transform was never clipped: at the end of a scroll its lower edge sat up to ~47dp below the hero's own item, painting a strip of banner at the hero's zoom into the gap above the first card - artwork that belonged to the top of the page appearing between the cards. The hero now clips its picture to its own bounds, so the page below it is the page and not a second crop of the key visual.\n- The progress wave holds its shape while it fills: The wave amplitude was read from the fill as it animated, so its whole length - including the part nobody has watched - inflated from a flat line to full height on every entrance and settled afterwards. The wave now stands at your progress from the first frame and only the coloured length springs to it, so the track is steady and the fill is the thing that moves.\n- The Nova numbers keep their place while they load: The four-number strip under the hero was drawn only once the detail response arrived, so opening a title showed the page without it and then pushed every card below it down when it appeared. The strip now reserves its slot while the page is loading, with its four labels in place and the numbers shimmering, and the real values land in the cells they already occupy.\n- My Entry opens at full height again: The editor overlay now opens to the full height of the window instead of stopping at a 60% peek, so the whole form is there in one place: status, progress, score, start and finish dates, the private switch, the note and the pinned Save and Delete bar. The sheet is measured once and moved in the draw phase, which also removes the squash the form used to do while it rose - the fields no longer re-flow and the action bar no longer slides under your thumb on the way up. Dragging the handle down still collapses it to the 60% peek, and dragging it back up or past the bottom settles it, all on the Motion style you chose.
- Delete and save ask before they write: Deleting an entry now opens an 'Are you sure?' dialog naming the title and stating that the progress, score, dates and note go with it, because AniList has no undo and the button sits one thumb-width from Save. Save changes asks the same way, and names the fields it is about to write, instead of sending the staged form on a single tap.
- Nova no longer flashes a blank page: The opening and closing transition is applied to the dialog's whole surface rather than to the content inside it. The surface is what paints the page's background, so fading only its children left an opaque rectangle of app colour on screen for the first and last frames of every open and close - the flash that read as the page failing to arrive. The entrance is now the window settling in over the list in both directions, and the editor overlay follows it.
- The Nova palette settles instead of switching: The cover's colour is read from the artwork after the page is already on screen, so the page used to open on the standing scheme and cut to the cover's a frame or two later. The scheme now eases between the two on the shared colour tokens, and the surface ramp is colour-corrected back toward your own theme by a small amount so a saturated cover cannot make the translucent cards glow or cost their captions contrast. Accents stay exactly the cover's, and Instant still changes in one frame because the colour tokens follow the Motion setting.
- The statistics drawer always opens fully: The score, popularity, favourites and length drawer is measured with the app's shared full-height sheet state. It could previously settle half-open on a tall distribution list, leaving the top of the drawer cut off mid-row with nothing to drag but the scrim.
